items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Notice of Motion
notes: Councillor Julie Wright – Support the Need for Provincial Action on Salt Pollution from Road Salt
Motion to be tabled March 24, 2025 for Council consideration April 14, 2025.

WHEREAS road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt;
and
WHEREAS salt levels in Ontario’s groundwater aquifers, creeks, rivers, and lakes have increasingly worsened since the 1970s, seriously affecting municipal drinking water sources and aquatic life; and

WHEREAS the City of Waterloo, in collaboration with the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, is actively attempting to mitigate salt pollution using existing policies, programs and site design measures that would be significantly more effective with supporting Provincial legislation; and WHEREAS the Ontario and Canadian governments have taken many actions over the past 25 years including setting water quality guidelines, developing voluntary codes of practice, signing the Canada-Ontario Great Lakes Agreement, and holding workshops, yet still the salt problem continues to grow; and

WHEREAS numerous situation analyses have recommended salt solutions involving liability protection, contractor certification, government- approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) and salt management plans; and

WHEREAS increased numbers of slips and falls claims, and other injury/collision claims related to snow and ice, are resulting in salt applicators overusing salt beyond levels considered best practices; and WHEREAS unlimited contractor liability is making it difficult or expensive for snow and ice management contractors to obtain insurance coverage, resulting in contractors leaving the business, thereby making it difficult for municipalities and private owners to find contractors; and WHEREAS the Snow and Ice Management Sector (SMS) of Landscape Ontario is working with the Ontario government to institute a limited liability regime for snow and ice management, including enforceable contractor training/certification and government-approved BMPs for salt application;
and
WHEREAS many Ontario municipalities have Salt Management Plans, but these often require updating considering improved science and better salt management practices now available.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. The City of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to work on a priority basis with key stakeholders to develop limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard BMPs for snow and ice management; and

2. The City of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to create and fund an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the province and municipalities on the best courses of action to protect freshwater ecosystems and drinking water from the impacts of salt pollution; and 3. This resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Conservation Ontario, Minister of the Environment Conservation and Parks (MECP), the Attorney General, and Premier Doug Ford.

items.title: Questions
notes: Mayor McCabe had a question for staff regarding sidewalk snow clearing, and how some properties don’t get cleared. She asked if this is something staff can look at for the next Winter, to ensure that people of all abilities are able to get around. Jim Bowman confirmed that he will look into it and get back to her on plans for next year.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Roe congratulated the students on Team DAVE at St. David Catholic Secondary School for winning at the University of Waterloo’s robotics competition over the weekend of March 20-22. Their team spirit and cooperation was fantastic to see.

Councillor Hanmer offered her congratulations to the University of Waterloo women’s hockey team for placing second in the 2025 Miller Waste Systems U SPORTS Women's Hockey Championship. She offered her thanks to Elmira for hosting the tournament, and to everyone who came out to watch.
Councillor Hanmer also mentioned that she’s been visiting Grade 5 classrooms promoting Council for a Day with the students. Some of them have some phenomenal ideas and are very excited.

Councillor Wright visited the Velocity Innovation Arena for the Future Cities Innovation Challenge Finals on Friday March 21. There were some great projects focused on municipal solutions that she’d love to discuss with staff.
Councillor Roe attended the 25th anniversary party for Steve Singer on Sunday March 23, who has been leading the basketball team for Special Olympics Waterloo Region.
Steve is an incredible community volunteer who has been engaged in so many different ways. It was a really great way to thank him and to have him hear the impact he’s had in the kids’ lives.

Mayor McCabe gave a shoutout to Wilfrid Laurier University, whose Faculty of Arts just celebrated their 100th anniversary on the weekend, with some of their award-winning professors sharing their work accompanied by musicians from the Faculty of Music.
